Under the MDR, any software that modifies physiological functions or provides treatment is classed as a Class IIa device unless it has a higher risk profile (e.g., if it delivers high‑dose medication or operates autonomously in a critical care setting), in which case it would be Class IIb. This classification is a prerequisite for both CE marking (or UKCA marking) and for any subsequent reimbursement or registration procedures in Germany.

CE marking requires that the manufacturer compile a technical file that demonstrates compliance with the essential safety and performance requirements set out in Annex I of the MDR, conduct a clinical evaluation per Annex II, and obtain a conformity assessment from an authorised notified body. For a Class IIa device, the manufacturer may use the “self‑declaration” route if it can demonstrate that all applicable general safety and performance requirements are met; otherwise, a notified body must review the technical documentation and issue a certificate of conformity. For a DiGA, the manufacturer must submit a dossier that includes data from randomized controlled trials or real‑world studies demonstrating therapeutic benefit, as well as an economic assessment showing that the intervention is at least as effective and less costly than standard treatment.
